_readMeFirst: This describes the CURRENT LOCAL-ONLY STAND-IN build, not the target architecture. The Streamarkr build plan's target is Vite + Cloudflare Worker + D1 (+ optional R2) + real provider adapters + GitHub CI. Everything below exists because this environment had no npm registry access — see AGENTS.md and docs/STREAMARKR_DECISIONS.md. Migrating to the real target architecture is expected future work, not forbidden.

targetArchitecture.status: not yet started — current build is a local-only stand-in, see currentToolchain below

currentToolchain.note: App runtime has no third-party runtime dependencies in this baseline. Repository devDependencies pin TypeScript and Playwright; a package-lock is still pending because the takeover runtime cannot reach npm, so initial CI uses npm install.

testRunner.tool: Node built-in node:test after tsc compilation
testRunner.installedAs: Node built-in; TypeScript compiler supplied by devDependency

browserQa.installedAs: devDependency: playwright 1.55.0; Chromium installed in CI

currentToolchain.todoWhenCiIsSetUp: Commit package-lock.json when a registry-enabled environment is available, switch CI from npm install to npm ci, then proceed with the planned Vite/Worker/D1 migration in focused builds.

testCommandExpandsTo: rm -rf test-dist && tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json && node --test test-dist/tests/*.test.js
lastKnownBrowserQaResult: Prior Claude run: 19/19 passing; GitHub CI browser QA pending first baseline PR
pendingIntegrations: Real streaming-service logo licensing (replacing src/ui/logos.ts colored-badge approach) — explicitly pending, not final
Commit package-lock.json and switch GitHub CI from npm install to npm ci once registry access is available
absoluteRules: No live network calls to any provider from this local build
No GitHub, no deploy, no Cloudflare from this build (this build only — migrating to them later is expected, not forbidden)
No real/personal data — synthetic fixtures only, including in any future live-provider test (use sandboxed/synthetic accounts, never production credentials)
No external npm runtime dependencies in the shipped app (the build/test toolchain is a separate concern — see currentToolchain above)
Never overwrite user-owned data from a provider-refresh code path
Never commit a real API key, OAuth secret, or credential of any kind
knownSchemaMigrationNotes: Current IndexedDB availability key [titleId, serviceKey] cannot represent multiple simultaneous option types for the same service; redesign this provider-owned table during D1 schema migration before live-provider integration.
